title: Playbook: security questionnaire-driven packaging and negotiation framework for SSO/RBAC commitments
creator: Aisha Khan
body:
Purpose:
Create a repeatable sales + legal + product playbook that ties answers to customer security questionnaires (SSQs) to deterministic packaging and contract concessions for SSO/SAML and RBAC requirements. The playbook should enable predictable negotiation outcomes, limit revenue leakage from ad-hoc concessions, and reduce time-to-close for enterprise deals that require SSO or fine-grained RBAC.

Background and context:
- Sales and Legal report frequent late-stage asks to: (a) include SSO/SAML in contract commitments, (b) mandate RBAC role models as contractual deliverables, or (c) request extended breach/availability/identity SLAs tied to identity integrations.
- Current handling is ad-hoc: concessions made per-deal, inconsistent terminology between Sales/Legal/Product, and unknown unit economics.
- Prior artifacts: PM-17423 pricing matrix research, ENG-2872 SSO integration backlog.

Problem statement:
- We lack a standardized mapping from SSQ answers to package level, pricing uplift, and permissible contract language. This causes: 1) revenue concessions without visibility, 2) longer legal cycles, 3) engineering scope creep during procurement, and 4) inconsistent customer expectations on delivery timelines.

Goals and measurable success metrics:
- Primary goal: Reduce time-to-contract for deals with SSO/RBAC asks by 30% within 3 months of rollout.
- Metric A: Median days from LOI to signed contract for SSO/RBAC deals (baseline 45 days). Target <= 31 days.
- Metric B: % of deals where concession is handled by standard package vs ad-hoc amendment. Baseline 40%. Target >= 80%.
- Metric C: Incremental ARR retained vs historical concessions. Target +5% ARR retention on large deals (> $200k ARR).

Experiment design (A/B style sales experiment):
- Variant A (Control): Current ad-hoc handling.
- Variant B (Playbook): Sales + Legal use the new questionnaire mapping and the three-tier concession ladder (Self-serve, Dedicated, Private) with defined uplift rates and standard clause language.
- Sample: Next 60 enterprise opportunities that surface SSO/RBAC requirements, randomized by region and ARR band.
- Duration: 90 days or until 60 samples collected.

Packaging & pricing recommendations (mapping examples):
- Level 1: Basic SSO & coarse RBAC (member/admin roles) -> Included in standard enterprise package. No uplift.
- Level 2: SAML + SSO custom domain + role templates + audit log export -> Included with 15% annual uplift or reserved capacity add-on discount.
- Level 3: Fine-grained RBAC (attribute-based roles, cross-tenant delegations) + contractual delivery SLAs & onboarding assistance -> Private deployment or Dedicated plan; 25-40% uplift + implementation fee.
- All levels: Offer optional KMS/HSM integration for keys as a paid add-on.

Contractual language & legal guardrails:
- Provide three approved clause templates: Basic SSO clause, RBAC functional commitment (deliverable + timeframe), and Implementation SLA (timeline, rollback, acceptance).
- Legal will accept these templates to reduce negotiation time; any deviation requires escalation to Legal + GC with documented business justification.

Sales playbook steps:
1) At qualification, Sales uses a standardized SSQ checklist (link below).
2) Map the customer's SSQ to Level 1/2/3, present the corresponding package and uplift.
3) Use the approved clause template in the term sheet.
4) If customer requests deviation, document the ask in the deal record and route to Legal for approval.
5) Post-signature: Create a Product onboarding ticket with the committed RBAC feature set and timeline.

Operationalization & engineering commitments:
- ENG deliverables required: SAML stability improvements (ENG-2872), RBAC role templates, audit export endpoint, and deployment runbooks for Private.
- Delivery timelines are tied to package level and must be included in playbook acceptance criteria.

Acceptance criteria for rollout:
- SSQ checklist implemented in CRM and visible on opportunity records.
- Three clause templates approved by Legal and staged in contract repository.
- Pricing uplift bands encoded in CPQ (or manual pricing guidelines until CPQ supports).
- Pilot with 10 deals completed; metrics captured and compared to control.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Engineering backlog unable to meet Level 3 timelines -> Mitigation: limited number of concurrent Level 3 commitments, prioritized by deal ARR and a non-refundable implementation fee.
- Risk: Customers push for custom language -> Mitigation: escalate and require business justification + signoff from Head of Sales.
- Risk: Revenue impact if uplift pricing deters buyers -> Mitigation: track win-rate, iterate uplift bands after pilot.

Timeline & milestones:
- Week 0-2: Build SSQ checklist and clause templates. Legal review.
- Week 3-4: Encode uplift bands and sales guidance; train AE team.
- Week 5-16: Pilot 60 deals (or 90 days). Weekly syncs to collect feedback.
- Week 17: Evaluate metrics, prepare roll/rollback recommendation.

Artifacts & links:
- SSQ checklist draft (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/SSQ-playbook-draft
- Clause templates (Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/enterprise-clauses/v1
- Engineering ticket tracker (Github): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/issues?q=ENG-2872
- Pilot dashboards (Looker): https://analytics.redwood.ai/dashboards/sso-rbac-pilot

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Q1: Do we require a non-refundable implementation deposit for Level 3 by default? Decision owner: Head of Sales.
- Q2: Should Level 2 require a minor annual minimum commitment to avoid churn risk? Decision owner: RevOps.
- Q3: Can we automate SSQ mapping in CRM using a webhook from the onboarding form? Decision owner: Platform Eng.

Comments and updates (chronological):
- 2025-06-15 (Aisha): Drafted playbook and shared with Legal for initial feedback. Linked SSQ checklist.
- 2025-06-18 (SOPHIE, Legal): Requested clearer acceptance criteria for RBAC deliverables and a recommended ramp schedule for Level 3.
- 2025-07-02 (Liam): Pulled engineering effort estimate for RBAC templates; flagged ENG-2872 as critical dependency.
- 2025-07-10 (Aisha): Added uplift bands and proposed implementation fee range ($25k-$75k) for Level 3.
- 2025-08-01 (Head of Sales): Approved pilot with 20 targeted deals initially. Requested weekly scorecard.
- 2025-08-15 (Liam): Confirmed CPQ can accept manual pricing entries; automation to follow in release console-2025.10.
- 2025-09-08 (Aisha): Updated metrics target after baseline re-evaluation; escalated Q1 to RevOps for final decision.

Next steps:
- Action 1: Legal to approve clause templates by 2025-09-15.
- Action 2: RevOps to finalize uplift bands and decide on Level 2 minimum by 2025-09-22.
- Action 3: Product/Eng sync to schedule Level 2/3 delivery windows (link to ENG-2872).

Acceptance notes for ticket close:
- Playbook must be published in Confluence and visible in the AE playbook library.
- Pilot run data and analysis uploaded to pilot dashboard and shared with Exec.
